article.name: DeepCode
article.summary: DeepCode's persistent project memory is a workspace-local set of Markdown notes. A bounded MEMORY.md index is loaded into new sessions, while the agent retrieves topic files through explicit list/read/write/append/delete actions. This review records source behavior at the verified main head; no system, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The official README describes DeepCode as an open-source coding agent with TUI, Desktop, Web and headless clients over a shared local service. Project notes are one part of session context alongside instructions, Skills and session history.

GitHub identifies main as the default branch. The official main Atom feed reports full head bfe34b668831848f144bb586f466e74b08846498, updated 2026-11-23T08:23:32Z; assessment source links pin that revision.

architecture.text: Persistent project memory is stored as Markdown files in <workspace>/.deepcode/memory/. MEMORY.md is a short index of topic links and hooks, injected into each new session with an 8,000-character cap; topic files hold longer notes and are fetched on demand.

The tool operates on regular files: list enumerates names, read fetches a named topic, write replaces contents, append concatenates, and delete unlinks. The offline Orient/Gather/Consolidate/Prune helper returns a candidate index and does not write it.

Project instructions in AGENTS.md, DEEPCODE.md or CLAUDE.md and user-level instruction files are separate from the persistent project-memory notes. A shared session builder supplies the memory integration across frontends.

behavior.text: Write requires non-empty content and creates the memory directory as needed. Append reads an existing file, trims trailing whitespace, adds a newline, and appends the new content. The tool does not add an automatic note-level revision history.

Write overwrites the prior file content. Delete removes the named file with unlink; the inspected path has no tombstone or recovery log. This is a source observation and does not establish removal from snapshots, backups, or copies elsewhere.

Retrieval loads MEMORY.md into the session prompt, then relies on the agent to list or read a named topic. The inspected interface does not offer keyword or vector search. Topic reads are bounded and refuse symlink targets outside the memory directory.

The MemoryTool receives a workspace path, stores notes under that workspace, rejects names that are not plain file names, and checks read targets against the memory directory. These code-visible filesystem boundaries were not tested as a deployment-wide tenant isolation guarantee.

The memory tool stores caller-provided text in ordinary files and does not attach typed source IDs, author, timestamp, confidence, or correction provenance. Any evidence trail depends on content supplied in the note.

The 8,000-character index cap and on-demand topic reads bound automatically injected memory context. The inspected memory path exposes no retrieval metrics, ranking, token accounting, or storage-efficiency reporting; none was measured.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval and abstention — unmeasured. No answer or abstention cases were scored.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured. No post-update factual probes were run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured. No post-delete probes, snapshot/recovery checks, or backup checks were made.
Scope isolation — unmeasured. No cross-workspace or cross-user probes were run.
Evidence support precision and citation coverage — unmeasured. No generated claims or citations were adjudicated.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay — unmeasured. No timed reads, writes, or recall probes were run.
Tokens, cost, and storage efficiency — unmeasured. No token counts, charges, corpus sizes, or disk usage were collected.

limits.text: This is a selected source review of the official README, Skills and memory guide, memory-tool implementation, shared agent-session assembly, and security policy at the verified head. It did not inspect every permission path, deployment mode, lifecycle, or backup behavior.

Memory quality depends on what is written into the notes and whether the agent follows the index to read a topic. Large-note behavior beyond the visible read cap, concurrent edits, practical isolation, and complete deletion guarantees remain unknown from this review.

The official README and SECURITY.md were checked for a contact email. Neither publishes one: the README directs bugs and feature requests to GitHub Issues and SECURITY.md directs vulnerability reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting. The record stores contact_email as null and these exact checked URLs.

benchmark.note: No DeepCode runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. Source observations, project metric definitions, and the benchmark fixture are not measurements for DeepCode.
